projects.name: claimsflow
projects.description: Conformance checking on synthetic motor-claims event logs. It aligns every case against the designed 11-step process, counts known rework loops and costs each one in days and money.
highlights: 50,000 claims and 610,616 events: 40 variants, and only 65% of claims follow the designed path.
The costliest loop touches 22% of claims and adds 4.4 days; total rework comes to GBP 4.5M a year.
A data-quality gate runs first, and measured loop rates match the planted ground truth.

projects.name: p2pexceptions
projects.description: Invoice exception analysis that assigns every failed three-way match exactly one cause, validates the assignment against labelled cases and ranks causes by cost.
highlights: 400,000 seeded invoice lines; 72,739 (18.2%) fail the PO, goods receipt and invoice match.
PO rounding is the top cause by count (39.5%) but fifth by cost; off-contract pricing leads by cost.
99.6% agreement with a labelled sample of 800, with unclassified exceptions always reported.

projects.name: permitflow
projects.description: A municipal permit workflow where illegal state transitions are rejected by the database, not by a service layer that another code path could bypass.
highlights: One statechart (11 states, 15 transitions, department SLAs) compiles into a transition table and triggers.
A raw INSERT that skips the service layer is rejected; all 95 illegal state pairs are refused.
Citizen-facing next-step text is generated from the same declaration, so it cannot drift.

projects.name: fieldextract
projects.description: Document field extraction with per-field calibrated confidence, routed to human review at a cost-optimal threshold.
highlights: Per-field isotonic calibration cuts expected calibration error 6x on held-out data.
Cost-derived thresholds spend the same 4,817 reviews for USD 18,518 instead of USD 32,896.
PII is redacted before any text reaches a model: 0 planted strings leaked across 500 documents.

projects.name: replayagent
projects.description: A single-node durable execution runtime for LLM agents in the style of Temporal. Every LLM and tool call is recorded in an event-sourced SQLite history, so a crashed workflow resumes without repeating finished work.
highlights: Retries with backoff, durable timers, human-in-the-loop signals and a versioning guard for in-flight workflows.
Real worker processes are killed at 8 crash points; a fresh worker resumes with identical results.
156 tests pass at 95% branch coverage, with zero runtime dependencies.

projects.name: pickpath
projects.description: An offline-first warehouse picking sync core. Conflicting picks that surface after pickers reconnect become supervisor exception tasks instead of being silently overwritten.
highlights: 500 induced double-picks produce zero silent losses and exactly one exception task each.
A last-write-wins baseline silently loses all 500 picks in the same simulation.

projects.name: previewd
projects.description: A Kubernetes controller that builds an ephemeral preview namespace per pull request from signed GitHub-format webhooks. It garbage-collects on close or TTL expiry.
highlights: Tested against a real kube-apiserver with envtest and a fake GitHub API.
The webhook path only records desired state; a pure-function state machine decides every action.

projects.name: provenance-gate
projects.description: A SLSA provenance verifier that checks signed attestations against policy, then rebuilds the artifact and diffs it. This proves the binary came from the reviewed source.
highlights: Rejects with 9 specific reason codes, from DIGEST_MISMATCH to NOT_REPRODUCIBLE.
Catches a compromised runner whose attestation is correctly signed and policy-compliant.

projects.name: pipeline-guard
projects.description: A reusable GitHub Action and CLI that gates pull requests on container-image vulnerabilities and IaC misconfigurations with a severity-weighted risk score.
highlights: On the vulnerable fixtures it scores 179 against a threshold of 30 across 21 findings and blocks the merge.
7 of those 21 findings are mechanically fixable by the auto-fix planner.

projects.name: rotationchaos
projects.description: A workload-identity lab that issues SPIFFE-style certificates with 60-second lifetimes and injects rotation failures. Every failure is asserted to fail closed.
highlights: Steady state: 50,000 requests, 1,666 rotations and 0 failures.
All 8 failure scenarios deny requests and fail closed.

projects.name: tfpolicy
projects.description: A Terraform plan policy linter that catches public buckets, world-open ports and wildcard-admin IAM before apply. It exits non-zero on any FAIL-severity violation.
highlights: Runs purely on plan JSON: no cloud credentials or Terraform binary at evaluation time.
On the bundled bad fixture it reports 8 violations (7 fail, 1 warn) and exits 1.

projects.name: kube-rightsizer
projects.description: Right-sizes Kubernetes workloads from real Prometheus usage history by opening a reviewable GitHub pull request against a GitOps manifests repo. It never mutates live objects.
highlights: Per-container recommendations from p95 usage plus 15% default headroom, with min/max clamps.
Surgical YAML patching that changes only resources.requests and resources.limits.

projects.name: pacingloop
projects.description: Real-time campaign pacing with hour-of-week median/MAD baselines and a damped, rate-limited controller. A hard spend ceiling is enforced outside the controller.
highlights: In the seeded simulator, 4 of 4 planted incidents are detected and classified, with 0.00 false alarms per week.
The damped controller makes 279 adjustments against 488 for a naive proportional one.

projects.name: upliftpolicy
projects.description: Retention targeting by uplift rather than churn propensity, evaluated with Qini curves and doubly-robust off-policy estimators. It surfaces the customers that contact drives away.
highlights: The top 30% by uplift adds 4.47 points of retention; the top 30% by churn score loses 0.23.
Sleeping dogs are 37% of the churn-ranked list and 4% of the uplift-ranked list.
